subproblem.title: Dominated convergence for the rescaled chart integrals
subproblem.statement: Let m, N ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝᵐ open, φ : ℝᵐ → ℝ^N continuous on V, J : ℝᵐ → ℝ continuous on V, L : ℝᵐ → ℝ^N a continuous linear map and v₀ ∈ ℝᵐ such that φ has Fréchet derivative L at v₀. Let c, δ, ε > 0 with B_δ(v₀) ⊆ V (closed ball) such that (a) c‖w‖ ≤ ‖φ(v₀ + w) − φ(v₀)‖ for every w with ‖w‖ ≤ δ, and (b) ε ≤ ‖φ(v) − φ(v₀)‖ for every v ∈ V with δ ≤ ‖v − v₀‖. Let f : ℝ^N → ℝ be continuous with compact support. With Hᵐ := μHE[m] on ℝᵐ, U_r := {u ∈ ℝᵐ : v₀ + ru ∈ V} and ψ_r(u) := r⁻¹(φ(v₀ + ru) − φ(v₀)), we have ∫_{U_r} J(v₀ + ru)·f(ψ_r(u)) dHᵐ(u) → ∫_{ℝᵐ} J(v₀)·f(Lu) dHᵐ(u) as r → 0⁺ (along 𝓝[>] 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m N : ℕ) (V : Set (Rn m)) (φ : Rn m → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) (J : Rn m → ℝ) (L : Rn m →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)) (v₀ : Rn m) (c δ ε : ℝ) (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N) → ℝ), IsOpen V → ContinuousOn φ V → ContinuousOn J V → HasFDerivAt φ L v₀ → 0 < c → 0 < δ → 0 < ε → closedBall v₀ δ ⊆ V → (∀ w : Rn m, ‖w‖ ≤ δ → c * ‖w‖ ≤ ‖φ (v₀ + w) - φ v₀‖) → (∀ v ∈ V, δ ≤ ‖v - v₀‖ → ε ≤ ‖φ v - φ v₀‖) → Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => ∫ u in {u : Rn m | v₀ + r • u ∈ V}, J (v₀ + r • u) * f (r⁻¹ • (φ (v₀ + r • u) - φ v₀)) ∂(μHE[m] : Measure (Rn m))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∫ u, J v₀ * f (L u) ∂(μHE[m] : Measure (Rn m))))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source (provenance only): steps 5, 6 and 7 (dominated convergence) of the parent proof, with J_φ replaced by an arbitrary function J continuous on V; the constants R, M and Λ are constructed below and (a), (b) are hypotheses, so the proof is self-contained.
Notation: g_r(u) := J(v₀ + ru)·f(ψ_r(u)), F_r := 1_{U_r}·g_r; B_ρ(p) is the closed ball.
1. Measure and base point. On ℝᵐ, Hᵐ = μHE[m] equals Lebesgue measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so we work with Lebesgue measure, which is finite on compact sets. Since δ > 0, v₀ ∈ B_δ(v₀) ⊆ V.
2. Constants. tsupport f is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B_{R₀}(0) for some R₀; put R := max(R₀, 1) > 0. Then f(y) ≠ 0 implies ‖y‖ ≤ R. Since f is continuous with compact support, there is M with |f(y)| ≤ M for all y (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). J is continuous on the compact set B_δ(v₀) ⊆ V, so there is Λ with |J(v)| ≤ Λ for v ∈ B_δ(v₀) (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). Also M ≥ |f(0)| ≥ 0 and Λ ≥ |J(v₀)| ≥ 0.
3. Indicator form. For every r, U_r is open (preimage of the open set V under the continuous map u ↦ v₀ + ru), hence measurable, and ∫_{U_r} g_r = ∫_{ℝᵐ} F_r (integral_indicator). So it suffices to prove ∫ F_r → ∫ J(v₀)·f(Lu) du as r → 0⁺.
4. Measurability. For every r, g_r is continuous on U_r: u ↦ v₀ + ru is continuous and maps U_r into V, J and φ are continuous on V (ContinuousOn.comp), u ↦ r⁻¹(φ(v₀ + ru) − φ(v₀)) is then continuous on U_r, f is continuous, and products of continuous functions are continuous. Hence g_r is a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to U_r (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable, U_r measurable), so F_r is a.e.-strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff). No measurability of g_r off U_r is needed.
5. Domination. Let G := Λ·M·1_{B_{R/c}(0)}. G is integrable: it is a constant on the closed ball B_{R/c}(0), which has finite measure (integrableOn_const, IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator). Let 0 < r < ε/R, so rR < ε; this set of r belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). We show |F_r(u)| ≤ G(u) for every u. If u ∉ U_r or f(ψ_r(u)) = 0, then F_r(u) = 0 ≤ G(u) because G ≥ 0. Otherwise v := v₀ + ru ∈ V and ‖ψ_r(u)‖ ≤ R. As r > 0, ‖ψ_r(u)‖ = r⁻¹‖φ(v) − φ(v₀)‖, so ‖φ(v) − φ(v₀)‖ ≤ rR < ε. If δ ≤ ‖ru‖ = ‖v − v₀‖, hypothesis (b) would give ε ≤ ‖φ(v) − φ(v₀)‖, a contradiction; hence ‖ru‖ < δ. Hypothesis (a) with w := ru gives c‖ru‖ ≤ ‖φ(v₀ + ru) − φ(v₀)‖ ≤ rR. Since ‖ru‖ = r‖u‖, this is r·(c‖u‖) ≤ r·R, so c‖u‖ ≤ R and ‖u‖ ≤ R/c, i.e. u ∈ B_{R/c}(0) and G(u) = ΛM. Also dist(v₀ + ru, v₀) = ‖ru‖ < δ, so |J(v₀ + ru)| ≤ Λ, and |f(ψ_r(u))| ≤ M. Therefore |F_r(u)| = |J(v₀ + ru)|·|f(ψ_r(u))| ≤ ΛM = G(u).
6. Pointwise limit. Fix u ∈ ℝᵐ. The map r ↦ v₀ + ru is continuous with value v₀ at r = 0, so v₀ + ru → v₀ as r → 0⁺. V is a neighbourhood of v₀, so eventually v₀ + ru ∈ V, i.e. u ∈ U_r and F_r(u) = g_r(u). J is continuous at v₀ (continuous on the open set V ∋ v₀), so J(v₀ + ru) → J(v₀). Next, ‖r⁻¹‖ → ∞ as r → 0⁺ (tendsto_inv_nhdsGT_zero composed with the norm), so HasFDerivAt.lim with the scalars r⁻¹ gives r⁻¹(φ(v₀ + (r⁻¹)⁻¹u) − φ(v₀)) → Lu; since (r⁻¹)⁻¹ = r this says ψ_r(u) → Lu. As f is continuous, f(ψ_r(u)) → f(Lu), so g_r(u) → J(v₀)·f(Lu), and because F_r(u) = g_r(u) eventually, F_r(u) → J(v₀)·f(Lu) (Tendsto.congr').
7. Conclusion. The filter 𝓝[>] 0 on ℝ is countably generated. Dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence with the bound G and steps 4–6) gives ∫ F_r → ∫ J(v₀)·f(Lu) du as r → 0⁺. By step 3 and step 1 this is the claim.
proof_key_steps: Hᵐ = Lebesgue measure on ℝᵐ; constants R (support radius), M = sup|f|, Λ = sup of |J| on B_δ(v₀)
∫_{U_r} g_r = ∫ 1_{U_r} g_r with U_r open; F_r is a.e.-strongly measurable since g_r is continuous on U_r
for 0 < r < ε/R: if F_r(u) ≠ 0 then (b) forces ‖ru‖ < δ and (a) gives ‖u‖ ≤ R/c, so |F_r| ≤ ΛM·1_{B_{R/c}(0)}
pointwise: u ∈ U_r eventually, J(v₀+ru) → J(v₀), ψ_r(u) → Lu by HasFDerivAt.lim, so F_r(u) → J(v₀)f(Lu)
dominated convergence along the countably generated filter 𝓝[>] 0

audit.reason: The signed-J generalization is valid because domination bounds |J|. The proof derives v₀ ∈ V, establishes restricted measurability, constructs an integrable fixed bound, and proves pointwise convergence using HasFDerivAt.lim. Filter dominated convergence yields precisely the stated limit; the two geometric estimates are explicit hypotheses.
